**Proposed mechanism:** KPTN (HGNC:29002) —DISRUPTS→ TORC1 signaling pathway (WP:WP403); NPRL3 (HGNC:19884) —DISRUPTS→ TORC1 signaling pathway (WP:WP403); TORC1 signaling pathway (WP:WP403) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); TORC1 signaling pathway (WP:WP403) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability, severe (HP:0010864). **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of KPTN and NPRL3 in TORC1 signaling could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both intellectual disability and epilepsy.

#### 3. autosomal dominant deafness - onychodystrophy syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.445)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6V1B2 (HGNC:11566) —DISRUPTS→ Vacuolar H+-ATPase function (GO:0005930); Vacuolar H+-ATPase function (GO:0005930) —LEADS_TO→ Deafness (HP:0000365); Vacuolar H+-ATPase function (GO:0005930) —LEADS_TO→ Nail dystrophy (HP:0001104); Vacuolar H+-ATPase function (GO:0005930) —LEADS_TO→ Renal Fanconi syndrome (HP:0001895); Vacuolar H+-ATPase function (GO:0005930) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP6V1B2 disrupt the function of the vacuolar H+-ATPase, a proton pump crucial for maintaining acidic pH in lysosomes and endosomes. This disruption leads to impaired protein degradation, lysosomal dysfunction, and cellular homeostasis defects, manifesting as deafness, nail dystrophy, renal Fanconi syndrome, and intellectual disability in both Koshino-Kawakami syndrome and autosomal dominant deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in ATP6V1B2 are found to be absent or extremely rare (gnomAD allele frequency > 1%) in individuals with either Koshino-Kawakami syndrome or autosomal dominant deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome, this proposed mechanistic link would be falsified. _(variant: rs755209363)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of vacuolar H+-ATPase dysfunction in these distinct syndromes could facilitate the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring lysosomal pH or mitigating the downstream cellular consequences, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 4. autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2C  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.444)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6V1E1 (HGNC:1095) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0015245); V-ATPase complex assembly and function (GO:0015245) —DECREASES→ Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000315); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000315) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue development (HP:0001063); Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000315) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP6V1E1 disrupt the assembly and function of the V-ATPase complex, leading to impaired lysosomal acidification. This dysfunction affects multiple cellular processes, ultimately manifesting as abnormal connective tissue development in cutis laxa and intellectual disability in MONDO:0014289.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in ATP6V1E1 who exhibit only one of the two disease phenotypes, or individuals with pathogenic variants in ATP6V1E1 that lead to a gain-of-function mechanism. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in ATP6V1E1 in gnomAD that are not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting V-ATPase activity or lysosomal function could offer a shared therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0014289 and autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2C. Understanding the specific downstream pathways affected by lysosomal dysfunction may reveal disease-specific therapeutic targets.

#### 5. renal tubular acidosis, distal, 2, with progressive sensorineural hearing loss  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.444)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6V1B1 (HGNC:9106) —DISRUPTS→ V-type proton ATPase activity (GO:0015011); V-type proton ATPase activity (GO:0015011) —DECREASES→ Acid-base homeostasis in renal tubules (GO:0001957); Acid-base homeostasis in renal tubules (GO:0001957) —LEADS_TO→ Renal tubular acidosis (HP:0001917); V-type proton ATPase activity (GO:0015011) —DECREASES→ Endolymph pH regulation in cochlea (GO:0001676); Endolymph pH regulation in cochlea (GO:0001676) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Mutations in ATP6V1B1 disrupt the V-type proton ATPase, impairing acid-base homeostasis in renal tubules leading to distal renal tubular acidosis, and also affecting endolymph pH regulation in the cochlea, resulting in sensorineural hearing loss.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis provides a potential avenue for developing targeted therapies that could address aspects of both renal and auditory dysfunction, or at least offer a unified diagnostic approach.

#### 6. autosomal recessive cutis laxa type 2D  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP6V1A (HGNC:1060) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005913); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005913) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue development (HP:0003073); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cutis laxa (HP:0011697). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP6V1A disrupt V-ATPase function, which is crucial for lysosomal acidification and extracellular matrix remodeling. **How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ATP6V1A with a consistent loss-of-function effect in both patient cohorts, and the absence of such variants in healthy individuals with similar phenotypes. _(variant: The absence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in ATP6V1A in gnomAD that are predicted to cause loss-of-function.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ATP6V1A in V-ATPase function and extracellular matrix homeostasis could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting lysosomal function or matrix remodeling for both osteogenesis imperfecta and cutis laxa.
